topics.label: Introduction and Learning Outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer opens the class by connecting cancer histology to cellular biology and outlining the session's key learning outcomes.

topics.label: Tumor Virology, Proto-Oncogenes, and Transformation Assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the discovery of transforming viruses led to the identification of cellular proto-oncogenes and experimental assays for testing cell transformation.

topics.label: Classification and Mechanisms of Oncogenes and Tumor Suppressor Genes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the major classes of cancer-associated genes and examine their genetic mechanisms in cell cycle regulation and mutant protein function.

topics.label: Forms and Molecular Mechanisms of Genetic Instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how defects in DNA repair pathways, replication proofreading, and chromosome segregation produce sequence and chromosomal instability in cancer.

topics.label: Multistep Progression, Hereditary Cancer Predispositions, and Clonal Evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how sequential somatic mutations and inherited genetic defects accelerate tumor development and influence clinical progression.

topics.label: Conclusion and Recommended Reading
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the presentation by reviewing the learning outcomes, suggesting a textbook, and previewing the next session.
